    ans = [0 for i in range(n + 1)]

    segments = []
    queries_with_index = []
    for i, query in enumerate(queries):
        queries_with_index.append((i+1, *query))

Segment tree is a balanced binary tree where every node except the leaf node contain the total sum of its left child and right child. Considered as a special case of balance search tree, segment tree can be used to solve many problems. For the 1345B - Array Modification problem, segment tree can be used to solve it. The same method is used in this problem, based on the solution in the following link: https://codeforces.com/contest/1345/submission/94518174 indicates that segment tree can handle this problem. The problem is more complex than just calculating the prefix sum of an array. It needs to calculate the prefix sum for different parts of the array after different operations are performed on the array. 
The segment tree can handle this situation well. In this solution, every query is stored in a segment with three numbers. The first number represents the time when the segment starts, the second number is the index of the segment, and the third number is the length of the segment. These three numbers sum up and then are added to the prefix sum. We use the cumulative sum property of the segment tree to calculate the prefix sum. For each query, the time i is added to the sum of the prefix sum between the previous query's time and time i, so a new segment tree is used for each query. This way, we can always get the prefix sum of the array between the time of the previous query and the time of the current query. The time complexity of this solution is O(q * log n), which is very reasonable.
